reason: Section 8 allows division of non-marital property when marital property is unreasonably impoverished or when marital division would otherwise be inequitable.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Division of non-marital property
proposedGroups.reason: Section 8 allows division of non-marital property when marital property is unreasonably impoverished or when marital division would otherwise be inequitable.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Court may divide property that is not marital property.

reason: Section 9 requires fair and equitable division of marital debts and consideration of tax consequences in property division applications.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Fair division of marital debts and tax consequences

evidenceText: Division of marital debts and consideration of tax consequences

proposedGroups.reason: Section 9 requires fair and equitable division of marital debts and consideration of tax consequences in property division applications.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Court must divide marital debts fairly and consider tax consequences.

reason: Section 10 lists property transfer, sale, payment, child trust, security, and adjustment-payment orders available in section 3 or 4 applications.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court orders for implementing property division
proposedGroups.reason: Section 10 lists property transfer, sale, payment, child trust, security, and adjustment-payment orders available in section 3 or 4 applications.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the orders the Court may make to implement property division.

reason: Section 11 authorizes interim orders restraining disposition or impoverishment and preserving property pending section 3 or 4 applications.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Interim preservation orders in property division applications
proposedGroups.reason: Section 11 authorizes interim orders restraining disposition or impoverishment and preserving property pending section 3 or 4 applications.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the interim orders available to preserve property pending division.

reason: Section 12 requires each party to file and serve a verified statement disclosing property and debts.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Financial statement filing and service
proposedGroups.reason: Section 12 requires each party to file and serve a verified statement disclosing property and debts.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the verified financial statement filing and service duty in marital property division applications.

reason: Section 13 allows the Court to keep financial statement information confidential where public disclosure would cause hardship.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Confidential financial statements

evidenceText: Order respecting confidentiality of financial statement

proposedGroups.reason: Section 13 allows the Court to keep financial statement information confidential where public disclosure would cause hardship.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Court may treat financial statements and cross-examination as confidential.

reason: Section 14 allows the Court to direct sale of charged property after application and notice to interested persons.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Sale to realize security or charge

evidenceText: Realization of security or charge on property

proposedGroups.reason: Section 14 allows the Court to direct sale of charged property after application and notice to interested persons.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when property may be sold to realize security or a charge ordered under Part 1.

reason: Section 15 abolishes the presumption of advancement between spouses and applies a resulting trust presumption with joint-tenancy and bank-account rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Resulting trust presumption between spouses
proposedGroups.reason: Section 15 abolishes the presumption of advancement between spouses and applies a resulting trust presumption with joint-tenancy and bank-account rules.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the resulting-trust presumption and joint-tenancy proof rules between spouses.

reason: Section 16 defines when property is a marital home, including mixed-use property and multiple marital homes.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Description of marital home
proposedGroups.reason: Section 16 defines when property is a marital home, including mixed-use property and multiple marital homes.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how property is identified as a marital home and how more than one marital home may result.

reason: Section 17 deems shares that entitle occupation of a corporate-owned marital home to be an interest in the marital home.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Corporate shares deemed marital home interest
proposedGroups.reason: Section 17 deems shares that entitle occupation of a corporate-owned marital home to be an interest in the marital home.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when corporate shares are treated as an interest in a marital home.

reason: Section 18 gives spouses equal possession rights in a marital home, subject to exclusive possession orders and domestic contracts, and states when the right ends.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Spouses equal possession rights in marital home
proposedGroups.reason: Section 18 gives spouses equal possession rights in a marital home, subject to exclusive possession orders and domestic contracts, and states when the right ends.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the equal possession right in a marital home and when it terminates.

reason: Section 19 separates restrictions on disposition of a marital home, remedies for contravention, and status of required consent.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: When a spouse may dispose of an interest in a marital home
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 19(1) lists the joinder, consent, release, court order, and authorization conditions for disposition.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the conditions that permit disposition of an interest in a marital home.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Setting aside a contravening disposition
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 19(2) allows a contravening disposition to be set aside except for value, good faith, and no notice.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a disposition made in contravention of subsection 19(1) may be set aside.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Consent does not give ownership interest
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 19(3) states that joinder or consent does not of itself confer an ownership right, title, or interest.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the legal effect of joining in or consenting to a marital home disposition.

reason: Section 20 combines equal net-proceeds entitlement, unequal division, setting aside transfers, and no-notice purchaser protection.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Equal entitlement to net proceeds from marital home disposition
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 20(1) gives each spouse one-half of net proceeds, subject to court order and domestic contract.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the default equal entitlement to net proceeds from disposition of a marital home interest.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Unequal division of net proceeds
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 20(2) allows unequal division of net proceeds if equal division would be inequitable based on listed factors.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Court may divide net proceeds from a marital home unequally.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Setting aside transfers and protecting no-notice purchasers
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 20(3) through 20(5) address setting aside transfers, deemed notice, and protection for value, good faith, and no notice.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when transfers may be set aside and when a later acquirer is protected.

reason: Section 21 gives a spouse with possession rights the same redemption or relief-against-forfeiture rights and notice entitlement as the other spouse.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Spouse redemption and relief against forfeiture rights
proposedGroups.reason: Section 21 gives a spouse with possession rights the same redemption or relief-against-forfeiture rights and notice entitlement as the other spouse.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the redemption, relief against forfeiture, notice, and payment-effect rights for a spouse with possession rights.

reason: Section 22 lists multiple court powers respecting marital home status, consent, notice, dispositions, registration, and preservation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Determining marital home status and extent

evidenceText: determine whether or not the property is or includes a marital home

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraph 22(a) lets the Court decide whether property is or includes a marital home and the extent of it.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Court's power to determine marital home status and extent.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Authorizing disposition or dispensing with notice

evidenceText: authorize a disposition of any interest in the marital home

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraphs 22(b) and 22(c) address authorization of disposition when consent is unavailable, incapable, or unreasonably withheld, and dispensing with section 21 notice.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Court may authorize a marital home disposition or dispense with notice.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Setting aside, discharging, and preserving marital home interests

evidenceText: direct the setting aside of any disposition of an interest in the marital home

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraphs 22(d) through 22(f) address setting aside dispositions, discharging registrations, and interim preservation orders.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Court's powers to set aside dispositions, discharge registrations, and preserve marital home interests.

reason: Section 23 combines exclusive possession order powers, temporary relief, preconditions, and termination on death.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Exclusive possession order powers
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 23(1) lists the orders available for exclusive possession, release of property, payments, household goods, and maintenance obligations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the orders the Court may make for exclusive possession of a marital home and household goods.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Temporary relief and threshold for exclusive possession
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 23(2) and 23(3) address temporary relief and the shelter or child-best-interests threshold.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when exclusive possession may be ordered as temporary relief and the conditions for making the order.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Death terminates specified exclusive possession orders
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 23(4) states when orders under paragraph 23(1)(a), (c), (d), or (e) cease.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which exclusive possession orders cease on death of either spouse.

reason: Section 24 allows discharge, variation, or suspension of specified orders after material change or when terms and conditions are no longer appropriate.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Discharge variation or suspension of orders
proposedGroups.reason: Section 24 allows discharge, variation, or suspension of specified orders after material change or when terms and conditions are no longer appropriate.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Court may discharge, vary, or suspend exclusive-possession-related orders or terms.

reason: Section 25 authorizes interim orders for delivering up, safekeeping, and preservation of the marital home or household goods.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Interim orders for marital home or household goods
proposedGroups.reason: Section 25 authorizes interim orders for delivering up, safekeeping, and preservation of the marital home or household goods.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the interim orders available for preserving a marital home or household goods.
